subject: Shiny Server Not Working Correctly After Uninstalling and Reinstalling

messages.author: 92c72466d9317b05
messages.subject: Shiny Server Not Working Correctly After Uninstalling and Reinstalling
parts:
Shiny server works upon first installation. After uninstalling and reinstalling, it works partially now.  On the Shiny Default home page (127.0.0.1:XXXX), the sample apps on the top and bottom left will not load now. I paste the log file error here.

/mypath/R/bin/exec/R: error while loading shared libraries: libicuuc.so.52: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

On the my own app page (127.0.0.1:XXXX/myapp), I have 

An error has occurred

The application failed to start.

The application exited during initialization.


Note that this seems like a dynamic library issue but its really weird because it didn't happen on fresh install. Whatever library (see underlined) I fixed, it just keeps popping for error on another library. In no particular order, I have also executed commands like LDCONFIG, export LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Some removal and installation of R also took place due to versioning matter.

This is definitely Shiny Server problem because I have tested shiny::runApp() and it works. Its just whenever the hosting is done by Shiny Server, the app will not load. I have restarted/reinstall Shiny Server too but nothing worked.

I am running on Centos6.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server Not Working Correctly After Uninstalling and Reinstalling
parts:
Turns out its an R installation path issue. In root mode, when i type R in terminal, I can launch R but this is not the case in normal user mode. In normal user mode, I get exactly the same error found in log file, i.e., error while loading shared libraries: libicuuc.so.52: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory. 
This means the path to R is not the same for both users (root and non-root user) and I have no idea why.

Troubleshooting and solution:
1. check that whether [which R@root] != [which R@normal_user], if true go to step #2
2. cp R in directory of R@root and overwrites the directory of R@normal_user with it (remember to backup first)

The reason for this hack is because those paths inside the script [which R@normal_user] are not the same as [which R@root]. I basically make the path [which R@normal_user] as a shortcut to [which R@root]. Any other solution is welcome. BTW, I have no idea why this happened. Probably I did some silly things because other languages like JAVA have congruent executable path among different users. One thing to note, the way I installed R on this centos6 machine is yum install R rather than build from source because my zlib on this machine is version 1.2.3 and version 1.2.5 is needed (even yum repo latest is 1.2.3) so it kinda failed on the configure step.
